openers.line: Before the debate begins, the contenders pray to protect each other.
openers.claimNote: Reflects the Śānti Pāṭha ethos where inquiry begins in non-adversarial safety.

openers.line: Resilience is not the art of bouncing back. It is the discovery of what never fell.
openers.claimNote: Distinguishes the Upanishadic paradigm of immutable Atman from modern elastic recovery.

openers.line: They left the sacrificial smoke behind to sit on the cold forest ground and ask who is watching.
openers.claimNote: Historical shift from ritual sacrifice (Karma-kāṇḍa) to interior inquiry (Jñāna-kāṇḍa).

openers.line: Fear needs a second. Remove the second, and fear has nowhere to stand.
openers.claimNote: Direct philosophical encapsulation of Bṛhadāraṇyaka 1.4.2 (dvitīyād vai bhayaṃ bhavati).

openers.line: Some twenty-five centuries ago, a boy asked Death a question and refused every bribe.
openers.claimNote: Cautious dating of Kaṭha Upaniṣad c. 5th-4th century BCE.

openers.line: The horses will break your neck unless the charioteer remembers who owns the carriage.
openers.claimNote: Vivid rendering of Kaṭha 1.3 senses (indriyas) vs intellect (buddhi).

openers.line: A scholar carrying encyclopedias into the woods, weeping because knowledge cannot cure sorrow.
openers.claimNote: Narrative snapshot of Nārada's confession to Sanatkumāra in Chāndogya 7.1.

openers.line: Drop salt in the vessel; stir the water; tell me where the salt ends and water begins.
openers.claimNote: Uddālaka's experiential experiment for Śvetaketu in Chāndogya 6.13.

openers.line: The cloud does not retaliate when the lightning tears through it.
openers.claimNote: Titikṣā as non-reactive, majestic endurance rather than numb suppression.

openers.line: You are not the garment. You are not even the skin beneath the garment.
openers.claimNote: Taittirīya kosha peeling from physical food sheath to innermost bliss.

openers.line: The storm moves the tree. It does not move the ground.
openers.claimNote: The foundational thesis of Dhairya and the two birds of Muṇḍaka 3.1.1.

openers.line: The arrow that trembles on the bowstring cannot pierce the darkness.
openers.claimNote: Muṇḍaka 2.2 bow-and-arrow metaphor for uncompromising mental concentration.

openers.line: Your mind is the weather. You are the sky.
openers.claimNote: Clear cognitive defusion parallel from Maitrī 6.34 on mind as cause of bondage.

openers.line: Work a hundred years without collapsing, because you stopped trying to own the outcome.
openers.claimNote: Īśā 1-2 synthesis of vigorous action without possessive entanglement.

openers.line: She pushed past the philosopher’s patience until he told her her head would split.
openers.claimNote: Historical record of Gārgī pressing Yājñavalkya to the cosmological boundary in Bṛhadāraṇyaka 3.6.

openers.line: Silence is not the absence of sound; it is the presence of an unshakeable attention.
Do not mistake an ancient text for your personal therapist.
openers.claimNote: Honest critical boundary against spiritual bypassing and modern misapplication.

openers.line: He waited three nights at a door nobody wanted to open, and walked out into the dawn.
openers.claimNote: Epilogue resolution linking Nachiketa's vigil to the sunrise prayer of Asato Mā.
